topic:
When normal confidence intervals work under Conflict Graph Design: a sharp degree frontier. For each n>=1 observe one design realization on n fixed labeled units with known simple undirected graph G and arbitrary-neighborhood-interference potential outcomes. Endpoint arrays a_i=Y_i(e_i), b_i=Y_i(0) define direct effect tau=n^-1 sum_i(a_i-b_i). H has adjacency I+A_G, lambda=lambda_max(H)>=1, D=max_i(1+deg_G(i)). Order each connected component by descending positive unit-norm Perron coordinate, ties by label; concatenate components by smallest label. B_i is the set of earlier neighbors. Independently sample U_i=1,0,* with probabilities 1/(4lambda),1/(4lambda),1-1/(2lambda). Fix r=2 and use published CGD Algorithm1 to realize E_ik={U_i=k, all earlier neighbors null}. Record U and observed outcomes. q_i=Pr(E_ik)=(4lambda)^-1(1-1/(2lambda))^|B_i|. T=n^-1 sum_i Yobs_i(1[E_i1]-1[E_i0])/q_i. For fixed B>=1 and 0<c<=1 impose n^-1 sum_i |a_i|^4<=B, n^-1 sum_i |b_i|^4<=B, and sigma²=Var_U(T)>=c lambda/n. Other potential outcomes unrestricted. No maximum-outcome bound or assumed CLT. All randomness is U. Define K_n(d;B,c)=sup over the specified fixed-design class with D<=d of sup_z |Pr_U((T-tau)/sigma<=z)-Phi(z)|, for integers 1<=d<=n. For each fixed B>=1,0<c<=1 determine an explicit necessary and sufficient growth condition on every integer sequence d_n for K_n(d_n;B,c)->0, including any essential slowly varying boundary factors. Derive a quantitative uniform normal-approximation upper bound and legal failure sequences proving necessity outside that regime. The formula/exponent is answer-open, not assumed. Strictly close the unresolved gap beyond the published sufficient d=o(n^(1/9)) condition, or show that condition sharp with a new legal obstruction. Defining the frontier by the original supremum or giving only a better unmatched sufficient exponent does not deliver the kernel. For W_ik=s_k 1[E_ik]/q_i (s_1=1,s_0=-1), let V=Cov_U(W), a known 2n×2n PSD matrix. VB=lambda_max(V)n^-2 sum_i(a_i²+b_i²); VBhat=lambda_max(V)n^-2 sum_i,k (Yobs_i)²1[E_ik]/q_i. Prove uniform VBhat/VB->1 in the normal regime and conservative coverage of T±z_(1-alpha/2)sqrt(VBhat) for each fixed alpha∈(0,1), with R fallback if VBhat=0. This estimates the conservative spectral variance bound, not the generally unidentifiable exact variance. Estimator algebra and class fixed; proof mechanism delegated. CONSUMER: DeclareDesign's published Research Design in the Social Sciences, section18.10/Declaration18.13, https://book.declaredesign.org/library/experimental-causal.html, implements the inquiry direct_ATE=mean(Y_1_0-Y_0_0) using the interference package for a lawn-sign/vote-margin design modeled after Green et al. (2016), The Effects of Lawn Signs on Vote Outcomes: Results from Four Randomized Field Experiments, Electoral Studies41:143–150. Its units are 238 Fairfax voting precincts; treatment is placement of candidate lawn signs, outcome is precinct vote margin, and the known undirected graph is geographic queen adjacency from poly2nb. The declared hop=1 model makes Y_i(e_i)=Y_1_0 and Y_i(0)=Y_0_0: signs in i with no neighboring signs versus no local signs. This is exactly this kernel's direct-effect inquiry, and the broader arbitrary-neighborhood class includes that exposure model. Changed practice: for future CGD replications of this SAME inquiry, replace the assignment/estimator by fixed CGD and use the derived degree rule to choose when its shorter Wald interval is justified rather than conservative Chebyshev calibration. The published declaration uses Bernoulli assignment and Aronow–Samii HT/Hajek, not CGD; no historical interval is retroactively validated, and the theorem gives an asymptotic benchmark rather than a finite-n certificate for the 238-precinct example.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fresh presolve derived an exact forward Doob decomposition of the fixed r=2 estimator. Oriented-adjacency interpolation controls the sum of fourth increments by C B n lambda D²; a prefix-product coordinate-flip bound and Bernoulli variance tensorization control quadratic-variation variance by C B n lambda² D. A classical martingale normal-approximation theorem then suggests the sharp condition d_n=o(n^(2/3)). Repeated Perron-ordered stars give a Gaussian-plus-centered-Poisson boundary limit while preserving the original endpoint fourth moments and variance floor. A separate second-moment argument supports the stipulated spectral variance-bound estimator and conservative Wald coverage. Seven finite graph-family enumerations passed; these checks are not a universal proof. Direct substitutions in recent generic dependency-graph bounds did not supply the same frontier.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit the general coordinate-flip envelope and its operator-norm chain in draft equations (4.1)–(4.4), alongside the imported martingale theorem; the proposed exponent remains unverified.
EARLY KILL TEST: Prove or refute equation (4.2) for overlapping parent prefixes and arbitrary signed endpoints, especially shared-parent bipartite graphs. Stop this exponent claim if repair requires stronger graph or moment assumptions; retain the original answer-open problem for reassessment.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_conflictgraph_uniform_clt_degree_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp necessary-and-sufficient maximum-degree growth frontier, including any essential slowly varying boundary factor, for uniform Gaussian approximation of the fixed r=2 Perron-ordered Conflict Graph Design direct-effect estimator under bounded endpoint fourth moments and a variance floor.

source_refs.claim: The CGD paper proves asymptotic normality under d_max(H)=o(n^(1/9)), describes this condition as partly driven by dependency-graph analysis, and gives a nonnormal example only in a substantially denser regime.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.claim: This paper sharpens Berry–Esseen bounds for sparse dependency graphs under finite L^delta moments, but does not exploit CGD's ordered prefix-product structure.
source_refs.author: Maximilian Janisch and Thomas Lehéricy

source_refs.excerpt: yielding a design-based Horvitz-Thompson CLT and oracle Wald coverage under a growing dependency degree
the new part is the ego-incidence primitive translation, not a new CLT frontier

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published o(n^(1/9)) condition treats unit contributions through generic dependency neighborhoods, causing degree and moment factors to compound, while the existing nonnormal construction does not determine the intervening regime. The prior ego-cluster proposal likewise supplied only a sufficient dependency-degree CLT. CGD exposure indicators instead contain overlapping earlier-neighbor null prefixes generated by a global priority order, so a sharp result must replace the ordinary support-overlap reduction by a prefix-sensitive argument and pair it with legal boundary counterexamples. The supplied n^(2/3) presolve candidate remains unverified and is not a literature fact.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit function R(n,d;B,c) bounding K_n(d;B,c) and tending to zero exactly under a stated growth condition on d, together with graph-and-endpoint sequences satisfying the same fourth-moment and variance-floor restrictions for which Gaussian approximation fails whenever that condition is violated.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from arbitrary neighborhood interference to estimand-specific design, spectral precision, and the unresolved inferential cost of maximum degree.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Desired exposures conflict under arbitrary neighborhood interference -> Perron-ordered CGD attains spectral-radius-controlled precision -> normal inference still requires the apparently proof-driven o(n^(1/9)) degree condition -> identify the exact degree frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply a martingale Berry–Esseen bound through simultaneous control of high moments of increments and deviation of normalized predictable quadratic variation from one.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Revealing the independent CGD coordinates in Perron order produces a Doob martingale, and the desired Kolmogorov bound has exactly Haeusler's two load-bearing inputs.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Stein couplings for dependency neighborhoods to bound normal-approximation error through neighborhood size and third- and fourth-moment terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the baseline machinery underlying the published CGD CLT, so comparison with a filtration argument isolates where the 1/9 exponent is lost.

method_exemplars.technique: Use smoothing and martingale replacement arguments that expose exact-rate obstructions caused by conditional-variance fluctuations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A sharp frontier needs both an upper rate and matching failure behavior, which is structurally closer to Bolthausen's exact-rate program than to a sufficient CLT alone.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove or refute the uniform coordinate-flip and predictable-quadratic-variation bounds required by a Perron-ordered Doob-martingale analysis of CGD when earlier-neighbor prefixes overlap, particularly on shared-parent bipartite graphs with arbitrary signed endpoints.

source_refs.claim: Algorithm 1 generates assignments from independent desired-exposure coordinates in an importance order, but the published CLT instead uses unit-level dependency neighborhoods.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.claim: Haeusler converts martingale increment moments and normalized quadratic-variation error into a quantitative normal-approximation bound and shows the dependence can be exact.
source_refs.author: Erich Haeusler

source_refs.claim: Chin obtains design-based CLTs under growing interference using restricted-degree dependency graphs and Stein's method, illustrating the prevailing nonsequential approach.
source_refs.author: Alex Chin

open_problems.why_unsolved: Although revealing independent U_i coordinates always gives a formal Doob decomposition, changing one coordinate can alter many later exposure indicators through overlapping parent prefixes. Consequently the predictable quadratic variation is a nonlinear random function of shared prefixes, and generic martingale theorems do not provide the necessary graph-uniform envelope. The first unresolved step is a deterministic coordinate-flip inequality or tensorized covariance bound that remains valid for arbitrary signed endpoint arrays under only an average fourth-moment restriction; failure on shared-parent graphs would invalidate the proposed martingale exponent without resolving the original answer-open frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving explicit uniform bounds for the fourth moments of the CGD Doob increments and the variance or L^p deviation of their predictable quadratic variation, sufficient to instantiate a martingale Berry–Esseen inequality, or a legal shared-parent graph and signed endpoint array disproving those bounds at the claimed order.

writing_exemplar.why: It defines the sequential desired-exposure construction and exposes the gap left by the usual dependency-graph CLT.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CGD is generated from independent ordered coordinates -> its estimator is a nonlinear function of prefix products -> unit-level dependency graphs discard this filtration structure -> establish or refute the filtration-specific bounds needed for sharper normal approximation.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate increment moments and normalized predictable-quadratic-variation deviations into Kolmogorov-distance control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed CGD proof has precisely these two probabilistic inputs; the new work is to establish their graph-uniform deterministic and moment bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Control departure from normality of a martingale through moment and conditional-variance discrepancies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational quantitative template for checking whether the proposed quadratic-variation estimate is sufficient.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bounded-increment examples and smoothing arguments to assess optimality of conditional-quadratic-variation terms in martingale Berry–Esseen bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If overlapping prefixes destabilize conditional variance, this obstruction machinery suggests how to turn that instability into a legal non-Gaussian sequence.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a quantitative finite-class uniform ratio-consistency theorem for the observable CGD spectral variance-bound estimator and conservative Wald coverage under exactly the sharp normal-degree regime.

source_refs.claim: The CGD inference section defines a spectral variance upper bound, gives an unbiased observed-outcome estimator, and obtains pointwise consistency and Wald coverage under its sufficient CLT assumptions.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.claim: Exact design-based variance is generally not consistently estimable under interference; the paper instead characterizes admissible estimable conservative quadratic-form bounds.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Joel A. Middleton, and Fredrik Sävje
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Variance estimation, studentization, and limit-law theory are outside the present theorem scope.
add a feasible Wald theorem using Vbar_n and separate pointwise conservativeness from uniform conservativeness

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published CGD result gives pointwise triangular-array stochastic control, whereas the requested class takes a supremum over all graphs and signed endpoint arrays satisfying fixed B and c. Pointwise consistency does not imply a uniform probability bound when rare large endpoints can align with low-probability exposure events. Moreover, exact randomization variance contains unobservable potential-outcome cross-products and generally cannot be consistently estimated, so the theorem must remain about the deterministic spectral upper bound and combine uniform ratio control for its plug-in estimator with a CLT standardized by the true variance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every epsilon>0, an explicit vanishing bound on the class supremum of Pr(|VBhat/VB-1|>epsilon), together with a uniform liminf coverage theorem for T±z_(1-alpha/2)sqrt(VBhat) and a formally harmless fallback when VBhat=0.

writing_exemplar.why: Its inference section cleanly distinguishes the inaccessible exact variance, the spectral upper bound, estimation of that bound, and conservative Wald coverage.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact design-based variance contains unobservable potential-outcome products -> CGD replaces it with an estimable spectral upper bound -> pointwise consistency supports existing intervals -> uniform validity over the fourth-moment design class requires quantitative ratio control matched to the sharp CLT regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent design-based variance bounds as estimable quadratic forms, separate PSD conservativeness from stochastic estimation error, and derive inference through the bound rather than the unidentified variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested CGD quantity is exactly a quadratic-form upper bound whose estimator, rather than the exact variance, must support coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the exposure-weight covariance operator norm to dominate variance and inverse-probability-weighted observed squared outcomes to estimate the resulting bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the fixed estimator algebra; the unresolved work is its uniform finite-class strengthening and synchronization with the sharp normal frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Diagnose anti-conservativeness of network-robust covariance estimators under heterogeneous effects and construct an adjusted design-based covariance estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a nearby proof template for separating a computable variance surrogate from true randomization variance and propagating the distinction into coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the shortest uniformly honest design-based confidence intervals attainable for the CGD direct effect in graph regimes where point estimation is consistent but Gaussian standardization can fail.

source_refs.claim: CGD provides conservative Chebyshev intervals broadly and shorter Wald intervals under a sparse-degree CLT, while its counterexample shows that consistency alone does not imply a universal Gaussian limit.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.claim: This paper develops conflict-graph-dependent design-based minimax point-risk bounds under arbitrary neighborhood interference, but does not characterize minimax confidence length in non-Gaussian CGD regimes.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, and Fredrik Sävje

open_problems.why_unsolved: Outside a sharp Gaussian frontier, the existing CGD counterexample prevents automatic use of a normal critical value but does not establish that Chebyshev calibration is minimax or rule out graph-sensitive randomization calibration. The prior clique-block proposal supplies a candidate information-theoretic route, but its Bernoulli simultaneous-exposure reduction does not transfer verbatim: under CGD the first proof step must derive the block-level sufficient observation and fuzzy alternatives under priority-resolved exposure probabilities. The main obstacle is therefore a least-favorable assignment-distribution characterization that respects both the fixed graph and the one-realization observation pattern.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax confidence-radius theorem over a stated non-Gaussian CGD regime, consisting of a computable interval with uniform randomization coverage and a matching expected-half-width lower bound for every uniformly honest interval, or a theorem identifying observable graph conditions permitting a strictly smaller critical value.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest practical framing of the tension between wide Chebyshev calibration, shorter Wald intervals, and the absence of a universal limit law.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Spectral design yields consistent estimation on many growing-degree graphs -> Gaussian calibration is shorter but can fail -> Chebyshev calibration remains valid but may be wasteful -> characterize the best honest interval available without a universal CLT.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nonasymptotic randomization confidence intervals using negative dependence or variance adaptivity and prove information-theoretic optimality through testing reductions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result likewise asks for a computable uniformly valid interval and a matching confidence-length lower bound, with CGD exposure revelation replacing ordinary treatment revelation.

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate design-based minimax risk over arbitrary-neighborhood-interference potential outcomes and derive conflict-graph-dependent upper and lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested confidence-radius characterization is the inference analogue of this point-estimation minimax program under the same fixed-potential-outcome assignment geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds and establish admissibility within a quadratic-form class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Any shortest honest interval must first eliminate avoidable slack in its computable scale before optimizing the critical value.

literature_map:
1. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) introduce Conflict Graph Design, prove variance O(lambda(H)/n), and construct a spectral variance-bound estimator.
2. Their CLT result assumes d_max(H)=o(n^(1/9)); the paper attributes part of this condition to dependency-graph proof limitations rather than claiming a sharp frontier.
3. Their nonnormal direct-effect construction lies in a substantially denser regime, leaving a wide interval between known sufficiency and failure.
4. Ross (2011, doi:10.1214/11-PS182) supplies the Stein dependency-neighborhood theorem used by the CGD analysis; Chin (2019, arXiv:1804.03105) applies the same broad strategy under interference.
5. Baldi and Rinott (1989, doi:10.1214/aop/1176991178) and Chen and Shao (2004, arXiv:math/0410104) are foundational quantitative local-dependence references.
6. Janisch and Lehéricy (2022, arXiv:2212.02590) improve sparse-dependency-graph Berry–Esseen bounds under finite L^delta moments, but do not exploit CGD's ordered coordinates.
7. Heyde and Brown (1970), Bolthausen (1982, doi:10.1214/aop/1176993776), and Haeusler (1988, doi:10.1214/aop/1176991901) make martingale increments and conditional quadratic variation the principal alternative route.
8. Searches combining Conflict Graph Design with martingale, Doob, quadratic variation, and Berry–Esseen found no published CGD-specific martingale frontier; the presolve n^(2/3) candidate remains unverified.
9. Aronow and Samii (2017, doi:10.1214/16-AOAS1005) establish inverse-probability estimation, conservative randomization variance estimation, and local-dependence asymptotic normality under general interference.
10. Leung (2022, Econometrica), Li and Wager (2022, arXiv:2007.13302), and Sävje, Aronow, and Hudgens (2021, arXiv:1711.06399) obtain network-interference asymptotics under structural or stochastic regimes distinct from the fixed-graph CGD supremum class.
11. Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2112.01709) formalize the general impossibility of exact variance estimation and optimize admissible conservative quadratic-form bounds.
12. Harshaw, Sävje, and Wang (2022, arXiv:2210.08698) give a general design-based Riesz framework with asymptotic normality and conservative variance estimation, but not a sharp CGD degree theorem.
13. Gao and Ding (2025, arXiv:2309.07476) show network-robust covariance estimators can be anti-conservative and develop adjusted design-based covariance estimators.
14. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) develop conflict-graph minimax point-risk bounds, advancing optimal estimation theory without settling Gaussian approximation or confidence-length frontiers.
15. The live tension is specific: spectral design removes maximum degree from point-estimation rates, while available normal-approximation results and obstructions still depend materially on degree or stronger stochastic assumptions.
